sDescription: English singer, songwriter, and musician Denny Laine passed away at age 79 in Naples, Florida, due to interstitial lung disease. Alongside The Moody Blues, he performed on the 1965 single 'Go Now', which reached No. 1 in the UK and No. 10 in the US. During a 1965 tour shared by The Moody Blues and The Beatles, Laine formed a friendship with Paul McCartney, who subsequently invited him to join Wings. Laine remained a permanent member of Wings throughout their existence from 1971 to 1981, contributing guitar, bass, and keyboards, performing lead and backing vocals, and collaborating with McCartney on songwriting, including the 1977 hit 'Mull of Kintyre'.

Jim Stewart, who established the influential southern soul record company Stax Records, passed away at the age of 92. Through his work leading Stax, Stewart signed and supported the career development of numerous prominent soul and R&B artists, such as Otis Redding, Carla Thomas, Albert King, and the Bar-Kays.

John Miles, a British rock music vocalist, guitarist, and keyboardist, passed away following a brief illness at the age of 72. He is best recognized for 'Music', his 1976 hit single that reached the top 3 in the UK. At the 2017 Progressive Music Awards, he received the 'Outstanding Musical Achievement' award.

A crowdfunding campaign succeeded in raising funds for a statue of David Bowie in the town where he initially performed as Ziggy Stardust. A total of over 650 individuals contributed amounts that surpassed the £100,000 target with 19 hours left before the deadline. The monument was planned for Aylesbury, Buckinghamshire, the location where Bowie first introduced his Ziggy persona.

Spotify launched a new website called Spotify Artists to address critics by disclosing payout rates to musicians. According to these figures, the streaming platform paid an average of $0.007 for each play. The company outlined its business model by noting that it had distributed over $1bn (£612m) in royalties following its launch in 2008. Prior to this, Radiohead vocalist Thom Yorke removed his music from the platform earlier in the year to protest artist compensation.

After spending 45 weeks at the top end of the UK charts, singer Adele's second album ‘21’ become the biggest selling LP in Britain this century, surpassing the late Amy Winehouse's 2006 LP ‘Back to Black’.

At the University of Virginia's John Paul Jones Arena, Phish performed the concluding concert of their 2009 Fall Tour. During the start of the opening set, a completely naked and erratic fan broke onto the stage. The individual approached guitarist Trey Anastasio, embraced him, and kissed his cheek. Security eventually chased the fan down after he completed three laps around the stage.

During a conversation with the British newspaper The Guardian, George Michael stated that he reduced his cannabis consumption, smoking 'seven or eight' spliffs daily rather than the 25 he previously consumed.

Robbie Williams issued an apology to Nigel Martin-Smith, the former manager of Take That, and settled on paying undisclosed damages following an allegation stated in a track. Through the song 'The 90s', Williams claimed that Nigel Martin-Smith had embezzled money from the group.

At a Christie's auction in New York, handwritten Beatles lyrics for an early version of Maxwell's Silver Hammer by Sir Paul McCartney fetched $192,000 (£97,000). The same sale saw a guitar belonging to Jimi Hendrix sell for $168,000 (£85,000), a notebook of lyrics by Bob Marley go for $72,000 (£36,445), and a poem written by Doors frontman Jim Morrison achieve $49,000 (£25,500).

Band Aid 20 began a four-week reign at the top of the UK singles chart with a fresh recording of Do They Know It’s Christmas?, marking the third instance of the track hitting No. 1. This updated rendition included Joss Stone, Busted, Chris Martin, Bono, Justin Hawkins, Dizzee Rascal, Tom Chaplin, Ms Dynamite, Beverly Knight, Will Young, Jamelia, Fran Healy, Sugababes, Dido, and Robbie Williams.

U2 achieved a two-week stay at No. 1 on the UK album chart with their ninth UK No. 1 album, 'How To Dismantle An Atomic Bomb'. Additionally, the band secured their sixth US No. 1 album by topping the US album chart.

Doug Hopkins, a co-founder, songwriter, and guitarist for the American rock group Gin Blossoms, died by suicide. The 32-year-old musician had battled mental health difficulties, especially as the group rose to prominence after their top-selling song, "Hey Jealousy."

Whitney Houston began a ten-week period at the top of the UK singles chart with 'I Will Always Love You', marking the longest duration at No.1 for a female artist. The track, written by Dolly Parton, was featured on the Bodyguard soundtrack.

The Jesus And Mary Chain faced a ban from a US music television program following blasphemy complaints triggered by displaying the band's name on screen. Although the CBS program requested that the group use the name JANC, the band rejected the proposal.

Former Go-Go's singer Belinda Carlisle achieved her first solo No. 1 on the US singles chart with 'Heaven Is a Place on Earth', which also reached No. 1 in the UK. Academy Award-winning actress Diane Keaton directed the promotional video, which includes an appearance by Carlisle's husband Morgan Mason.

Fat Larry James, drummer, singer and leader of Fat Larry’s Band died of a heart attack aged 38. Scored the 1982 UK No.2 single 'Zoom'. The opening drum break from Down On The Avenue, from the band's first album, Feel It has been sampled by N.W.A. Ice-T, Jungle Brothers and Run-D.M.C.

Julio Iglesias reached No.1 on the UK singles chart with 'Begin The Beguine.' The track, featuring Spanish lyrics set to a 1935 Cole Porter composition, marked the singer's sole chart-topping single in the UK.

Prior to a Houston show, an off-duty police officer detained Stevie Ray Vaughan in a dressing room after seeing him consume cocaine near an open window. Following a formal cocaine possession charge, he posted $1,000 bail and was released. A subsequent sentence placed Vaughan on two years of probation with a travel restriction barring him from leaving Texas.

The debut single 'Anarchy In The UK' by the Sex Pistols received a review from the music weekly NME, which stated that "Johnny Rotten sings flat, the song is laughably naive, and the overall feeling is of a third-rate Who imitation."

Paul McCartney and Wings put out Band On The Run, marking his fifth album following his exit from The Beatles. A pair of successful singles from the record, 'Jet' and 'Band on the Run', established it as McCartney's most triumphant album. Most of Band on the Run was tracked at EMI's studio located in Lagos, Nigeria, because McCartney wished to record a record in a foreign destination. McCartney entered the studio accompanied solely by his wife Linda and Denny Laine, performing extra duties on drums, percussion, and the majority of the lead guitar sections himself alongside bass.

Judy Collins recorded the Christian hymn "Amazing Grace", featuring lyrics by English poet and clergyman John Newton that were first published in 1779. Her version entered the UK singles chart for the first of eight times, accumulating a total of 67 weeks on the chart without reaching the No. 1 position.

A London party marked the release of the Rolling Stones album Beggars Banquet. The gathering's main event was a custard pie food fight, and the occasion proceeded without any trouble for Keith Richards. Initially, the LP featured a plain white invitation design for its cover, though this was subsequently altered.

This was the final night of a 16-date UK package tour with Jimi Hendrix, Pink Floyd, The Move, The Nice, The Outer Limits, The Erie Apparent and Amen Corner at Green's Playhouse, Glasgow. All performances had two shows per night, in this case at 6.15pm, with the second at 8.45pm. Jimi Hendrix had the curtains closed on him halfway through his set, after the management at the venue regarded his movements with his guitar as having sexual overtones.

The Beatles played their last ever show in their hometown of Liverpool when they appeared at The Liverpool Empire during the group's final UK tour. Only 5,100 tickets were available, but there were 40,000 applications for tickets. The group also had the UK No.1 single with 'We Can Work It Out / Day Tripper.'

Beach Boys began a four-week stint at the top of the US album chart with their debut US No.1 release, 'Beach Boys Concert'. Captured live at the Memorial Auditorium in Sacramento, California, the LP stands as one of the rare official long-playing live recordings featuring the original lineup of the group.

Lorne Greene, the star of the NBC television series 'Bonanza', achieved the No. 1 spot on the US singles chart with 'Ringo'. This made him the second Canadian, following Paul Anka, to secure a US No. 1 single. Additionally, the track reached No. 22 on the UK chart.

Following an arrest for attaching a condom to a brick wall and setting it on fire, Paul McCartney and Pete Best were ordered to depart Germany, prompting The Beatles to head back home in a discouraged state.

'G.I. Blues' marked the fifth US No.1 album for Elvis Presley, beginning a ten-week reign atop the US album chart. The soundtrack featured tracks that were previously included in the motion picture sharing the same title.
Conan Gray is an American singer, songwriter, and former YouTuber. His 2020 studio album Kid Krow opened at No. 5 on the US Billboard 200, which marked the largest debut for a US artist that year.

American singer and songwriter Keri Hilson has composed tracks for performers such as Britney Spears, The Pussycat Dolls, and Mary J. Blige as part of the production and songwriting collective The Clutch. Her career breakthrough arrived in 2007 following a guest appearance on Timbaland's single "The Way I Are", which achieved chart-topping success internationally.

Zainam Higgins is a singer in the British girl group Cleopatra, known for the 1998 UK No. 3 single 'Cleopatra's Theme'. Madonna signed the group to her Maverick label and presented them to American audiences at Nickelodeon's 11th Annual Kids' Choice Awards, where the members performed their debut single, 'Cleopatra's Theme'. Following the performance, the track was released and climbed to No. 26 on the Billboard Hot 100.

David Hodges is an American songwriter and record producer. He co-wrote material on the Evanescence demo CD Origin in 2000 and their debut album Fallen in 2003. Alongside this, he has shared writing and production credits for various acts such as Kelly Clarkson, Celine Dion, Daughtry, Backstreet Boys, Avril Lavigne, David Archuleta, Christina Aguilera, Carrie Underwood, Jessie James, 5 Seconds of Summer, Christina Perri, and Tim McGraw. Among his works, he co-wrote David Archuleta's track 'Crush', which climbed to No. 2 on the Billboard Hot 100.

Craig Gill was the drummer for the English alternative rock band Inspiral Carpets, which achieved a UK No.14 single in 1990 with 'This Is How It Feels'. He conducted musical tours around the Manchester area that highlighted landmarks connected to the Madchester scene and the city's musical legacy. Additionally, he co-authored the book The Manchester Musical History Tour. Gill passed away at age 44 on 22 November 2016.
American R&B singer Michel'le released her self-titled debut album in 1989, which was led by the US Top 10 single 'No More Lies'. Dr. Dre provided guest vocals for the track.

Johnny Rzeznik works as a singer and guitarist for the American rock band Goo Goo Dolls. The group is well-known for their single 'Iris', released in 1998, which remained on the Billboard Hot 100 for 11 consecutive months and held the number-one position on the Hot 100 Airplay chart for 18 weeks.
Les Nemes played bass for Haircut 100. Between 1981 and 1982, the group achieved four UK Top 10 hit singles, which included 'Favourite Shirts (Boy Meets Girl)', 'Love Plus One', and 'Fantastic Day'.

American rock vocalist Jack Russell was a founding member of the hard rock band Great White, which scored a 1989 hit with a cover of Ian Hunter's song 'Once Bitten Twice Shy'. Russell passed away on 7 August 2024 at the age of 63.

American musician, songwriter, singer, and guitarist Jim Messina was part of Buffalo Springfield, which landed the 1967 US No.17 single 'For What It's Worth'. Following the breakup of Buffalo Springfield, Messina teamed up with Buffalo Springfield founding member Richie Furay to establish Poco in 1968. Later, as part of the soft rock duo Loggins and Messina, he achieved the 1972 US No.4 single 'Your Mama Don't Dance'.
British bass guitarist, Rick Wills. He is best known for his work with Foreigner and his associations with the Small Faces Peter Frampton and Bad Company.

Kim Simmonds was a Welsh rock singer and musician. As the sole consistent member of the blues rock band Savoy Brown, he played and appeared on every album the group recorded. He passed away on 13 December 2022 at the age of 75.

Canadian pop rock singer and songwriter Andy Kim achieved a 1974 US No.1 and UK No.2 single with 'Rock Me Gently'. He also co-wrote 'Sugar Sugar' in 1968, performing vocals on the track as a member of the Archies. The song held the No.1 position in the USA for four weeks and was named "Record of the Year" for 1969.

Eddie Serrato played drums for ? & The Mysterians, known for their 1966 single '96 Tears', which reached No. 1 in the US and No. 37 in the UK. The track was later a hit for The Stranglers in 1990. Serrato passed away at the age of 65 following a heart attack on February 24, 2011.

Frank Wilson worked as an American songwriter, singer, and record producer. During his time with Motown Records, Wilson created and produced successful tracks for Brenda Holloway, Marvin Gaye, the Supremes, the Miracles, the Four Tops, the Temptations, Eddie Kendricks, among others. Wilson passed away on September 27, 2012, in Duarte, California, following a prolonged struggle with prostate cancer, at age 71.

JJ Cale was a US guitarist and singer-songwriter. Other musicians have covered songs written by Cale, including 'After Midnight' by Eric Clapton, Phish, and Jerry Garcia; 'Cocaine' by Eric Clapton; 'Clyde' by Waylon Jennings and Dr. Hook; and 'Call Me the Breeze' by Lynyrd Skynyrd, John Mayer, Johnny Cash, Bobby Bare, and Eric Clapton. Cale died on 26th July 2013 of a heart attack.

Richard Penniman, an American musician, singer, and songwriter known as Little Richard, scored the 1956 US No. 6 and 1957 UK No. 3 single 'Long Tall Sally', along with more than 10 other Top 40 singles across the US and UK. His work was instrumental in developing other popular music styles such as soul and funk, and helped define rhythm and blues for future generations. He passed away from bone cancer on 9 May 2020 at 87 years old.

Sonny Boy Williamson II was an American blues harmonica player, singer and songwriter. Before adopting the name Sonny Boy Williamson, he performed under several aliases, such as Rice Miller and Little Boy Blue. Numerous rock and blues musicians have recorded his material, including Van Morrison, The Who, The Animals, Yardbirds and Moody Blues. He passed away on 25th May 1965.
